This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Hi-hat: open off-beats**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Drum grooves](index.qmd#drums)

## The pattern

Four on the floor: kick on every beat, snare on 2 and 4, a closed hi-hat on each beat and an open one on every off-beat (the stick closing it each time). The Four on the floor groove without the clap.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*, *Piano ballad*, *Acoustic strum*, *Dance pop* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the dance pop style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: open off-beats","opts":{"groove":"hhdance"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Hi-hat: eighth notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every eighth note, all of one weight, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The basic rock beat. In 3/4: six eighths, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums-hheighths.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Hi-hat: off-beats only

The closed hi-hat plays only the ands, 1-and 2-and 3-and 4-and. Kick on every beat, snare on 2 and 4. In 3/4: kick on 1 and 2, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums-hhoffbeats.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: off-beats only","opts":{"groove":"hhoffbeats"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Hi-hat: open off-beats, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Four on the floor: kick every beat, snare on 2 and 4, a closed hat on each beat and an open one on every and. The foot opens and closes in eighths.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: open off-beats","opts":{"groove":"hhdance"}},{"label":"Hi-hat: off-beats only (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"hhoffbeats"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

## How it relates to the other patterns

- **Leads to:** [Four on the floor](drums-dance.qmd): the patterns that use this one as a step.

- **Other drum grooves in the Folk, rock and pop group:** [Bo Diddley beat](drums-bodiddley.qmd), [Waltz in one](drums-waltz.qmd), [Two-beat](drums-boomchick.qmd), [Rock backbeat](drums-rock.qmd), [Pop backbeat](drums-strum.qmd), [Ballad](drums-ballad.qmd), [Four on the floor](drums-dance.qmd), [Motown](drums-motown.qmd).
